title: Chapter 6: Human Computer Interaction
description: Model–View–Controller (MVC) is a design pattern in Human–Computer Interaction and software design that divides a system into Model, View, and Controller components to make programs easier to build, understand, and fix.
content:
Overview of Model–View–Controller (MVC)

Model–View–Controller (MVC) is a design pattern in Human–Computer Interaction (HCI) and software design.

It divides a system into three parts:

  • Model – the brain (data & logic)
  • View – the face (what you see)
  • Controller – the hands (what you do)

Purpose: To make programs easier to build, understand, and fix.

MVC Restaurant Analogy

Think of MVC like a restaurant:

  • Model = kitchen (where the food is prepared = data/logic)
  • View = menu + food served (what the customer sees)
  • Controller = waiter (takes your order and delivers it between kitchen and you)

Components of MVC

1. Model (The Brain of the System)

Stores and manages the system’s data and rules.

Function:

  • Knows everything about the system’s content.
  • Updates data when something changes.
  • Does not care about how things look on screen.
  • Without the Model, the program has no knowledge to show.

2. View (The Face of the System)

The visual representation of the data.

Function:

  • Shows information to the user in a friendly way.
  • Changes automatically when the Model updates.
  • Without the View, users can’t see or interact with the data.

3. Controller (The Hands of the System)

Acts as a bridge between the user and the system.

Function:

  • Takes input from the user (clicks, taps, voice, typing).
  • Decides what action to perform.
  • Tells the Model or View what to do.
  • Without the Controller, the user cannot communicate with the system.

How MVC Works Together (Flow)

  1. User does something (click, tap, type) -> handled by Controller.
  2. Controller updates the Model (changes data).
  3. Model notifies the View of changes.
  4. View shows the updated information to the User.

Benefits of MVC

  • Separation of roles: Each part has its own job.
  • Easy to maintain: Designers can work on View, programmers on Model.
  • Reusability: One Model can work with different Views.
  • Flexibility: Changes in one part don’t break the others.

Quick Analogy Recap

  • Restaurant: Kitchen (Model), Waiter (Controller), Served food (View).
  • Human body: Brain (Model), Hands (Controller), Face (View).
  • Music app: Song data (Model), Playlist screen (View), Play button (Controller).

Remember: MVC is like teamwork. Each part has its own responsibility, and together they make the system run smoothly.
